title: Hereditary discrepancy and factorization norms (AimPL) — Problem 1.65: Tusnády's problem

problems.sourceStatement: Let $d_n$ be the discrepancy of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ wrt all alix-aligned rectangles i.e. the set system comprises of all axis-aligned rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^2$ as sets, maximised over all choices of $n$ points. Tusnady's problem then asks for the exact value of $d_n$. We can also ask for the same question in $\mathbb{R}^d$.
problems.problem: Determine the exact discrepancy $d_n$ of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with respect to all axis-aligned rectangles (the maximum over all $n$-point sets of the combinatorial discrepancy of the set system of axis-parallel rectangles), and the analogous quantity in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to axis-parallel boxes.
problems.wordDescription: Tusnády's problem (posed by Tusnády in the early 1980s) asks for the tight value of the combinatorial discrepancy of axis-parallel rectangles: given $n$ points in the plane, 2-color them so that every axis-parallel rectangle contains nearly equal numbers of red and blue points, and minimize the worst imbalance. In dimension 2 the discrepancy is known to be $\Theta(\log n)$-ish but the exact growth is open: Schmidt's lower bound $\Omega(\log n)$ (via Lebesgue-measure discrepancy, combined with a reduction of Beck) is the best known, while the best upper bound progressed from $O(\log^{2.5} n)$ to $O(\log^2 n)$ (Bansal-Garg 2017). In higher dimensions $\mathbb{R}^d$, Matoušek-Nikolov-Talwar proved $\Omega(\log^{d-1} n)$ (improving the previous $\approx \log^{(d-1)/2} n$) and $O(\log^{d+1/2} n)$, and Nikolov later improved the upper bound to $O(\log^{d-0.5} n)$; closing the gap between $\log^{d-1}$ and $\log^{d-0.5}$ remains open for $d \geq 3$.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Let $\mathcal{R}_d$ be the family of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and define $d_n^{(d)} = \max_{P: |P| = n} \mathrm{disc}(P, \mathcal{R}_d) = \max_{P} \min_{\chi: P \to \{\pm 1\}} \sup_{R \in \mathcal{R}_d} \left|\sum_{p \in P \cap R} \chi(p)\right|$. Tusnády's problem asks for the exact value of $d_n := d_n^{(2)}$ (and of $d_n^{(d)}$). Known: $d_n^{(2)} = \Omega(\log n)$ and $O(\log^2 n)$; $d_n^{(d)} = \Omega(\log^{d-1} n)$ and $O(\log^{d-0.5} n)$.

literature.title: J. Matoušek, A. Nikolov, K. Talwar, Factorization norms and hereditary discrepancy, IMRN 2020(3):751-790 (arXiv:1408.1376)
literature.description: Proves the $\Omega(\log^{d-1} n)$ lower bound for the $d$-dimensional Tusnády problem (improving the previous $\approx \log^{(d-1)/2} n$) and gives a new simple proof of the $O(\log^{d+1/2} n)$ upper bound.

literature.title: A. Nikolov, Tighter bounds for the discrepancy of boxes and polytopes, SoCG 2017
literature.description: Improves the upper bound for axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$ to $O(\log^{d-0.5} n)$, currently the strongest known upper bound for Tusnády's problem in higher dimensions.

literature.title: N. Bansal, S. Garg, Algorithmic discrepancy beyond partial coloring, STOC 2017 (arXiv:1611.01805)
literature.description: Gives an algorithmic $O(\log^2 n)$ bound for axis-parallel rectangles in the plane (improving $O(\log^{2.5} n)$) and $O_d(\log^d n)$ for $d$-dimensional boxes.

literature.title: W. M. Schmidt, Irregularities of distribution VII, Acta Arithmetica 21:45-50, 1972; J. Beck, Roth's estimate of the discrepancy of integer sequences is nearly sharp, Combinatorica 1(4):319-325, 1981
literature.description: Schmidt's $\Omega(\log n)$ lower bound on Lebesgue-measure discrepancy in the plane together with Beck's reduction yields the $\Omega(\log n)$ lower bound for Tusnády's problem in $\mathbb{R}^2$; this remains the best known lower bound in the plane.

literature.title: Discrepancy Theory: An Algorithmic and Geometric Perspective, arXiv:2608.00140, 2026
literature.description: Recent survey confirming the state of the art for Tusnády's problem: lower bound $\Omega(\log^{d-1} n)$ (MNT) and strongest upper bound $O(\log^{d-0.5} n)$ (Nikolov).

problems.verificationNotes: Verified on 2026-08-25. The page's status line contains a typo: the $\mathbb{R}^2$ lower bound should be $\Omega(\log n)$ (not $O(\log n)$); this is confirmed by the literature (Schmidt + Beck). The $\mathbb{R}^2$ upper bound $O(\log^{2.5} n)$ was later improved to $O(\log^2 n)$ by Bansal-Garg (STOC 2017). In $\mathbb{R}^d$ the page's upper bound $\log^{d+1/2} n$ was later improved to $\log^{d-0.5} n$ by Nikolov (SoCG 2017), per the survey arXiv:2608.00140. The problem remains open; in particular the exact value of $d_n$ in the plane is unknown.
problems.statusDetails: In $\mathbb{R^2}$, we know a lower bound of $O(\log n)$ on $d_n$ and an upper bound of $O(\log^{2.5}n)$. In $\mathbb{R}^d$, we know that $d_n\in[\log^{d-1}n,log^{d+1/2}n]$.
